title: regulatory-sprint-sell-card-compact-wip
content:
Purpose:
A compact battlecard / demo-deck cheat-sheet for selling short regulatory pilots to platform and security teams. Focus: quickly prove data isolation, auditability, and predictable economics with a minimal pilot (2–4 weeks).

Audience:
- Platform engineering (primary)
- Security/compliance leads (secondary)
- Buyer personas: Head of Platforms, CISO, Data Privacy Lead, ML infra manager

TL;DR (one-sentence opener for SEs):
We can run your pilot in a customer-controlled VPC or on-prem package with KMS-integrated keys, full audit logs, and an SLA-backed path to Dedicated capacity — so you get model fidelity without giving up control over data, keys, or networking.

Playbook (2-week focused pilot):
Week 0: Kickoff (1 day)
- Align scope: 3 sample flows, privacy OKRs, success metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy regression threshold).
- Confirm infra: VPC peering vs. VPN vs. on-prem. Identify required GPUs (A100 vs. H100) and expected throughput.

Week 1: Standup (3–5 days)
- Provision private control plane (or on-prem bundle) + KMS/HSM integration (test key rotation).
- Deploy 1 model variant (quantized option) and an autoscale rule for pilot load.
- Enable audit logging, SAML/SCIM for team access.
- Run initial smoke tests: token rate, latency, KV cache warmup.

Week 2: Validate & Handoff (3–5 days)
- Run benchmark scenarios (p95 latency, end-to-end response times under concurrent sessions).
- Execute a simulated failover: throttle primary region, show automatic routing to fallback model/region within Xs.
- Collect logs/trace links; share evaluation report and cost projection.

Technical checklist for SE/demo:
- Networking: confirm CIDR, peering/managed NAT, allowlist of Redwood egress IPs (if needed).
- Auth/Keys: KMS key ARN, rotation cadence, HSM requirements.
- Data residency: region(s) for model hosting + storage retention policy.
- Audit & retention: duration, S3/BigQuery export path, SIEM integration.
- Rollout: canary % and rollback policy for model updates.

Key metrics to show in demo (prep slide):
- P50/P95 generation latency (ms) at pilot QPS, tokens/s throughput, cold vs warm KV cache.
- Unit cost estimate: $/1k tokens (hosted) vs. $/hr for Dedicated — show delta and threshold where Dedicated makes sense.
- Failover demonstration results: mean failover time, error rate delta.

Canned sales script snippets (short):
- "For regulated workloads, we keep the control plane separate and keys in your KMS — you never hand us plaintext keys."
- "We’ll demonstrate an audit trail export within 24 hours so your compliance team can ingest logs into your SIEM."
- "If latency or cost needs tighten, we’ll show a quantized variant and batching config that trades <2% quality for ~40% lower cost."

Common objections + responses:
- Objection: "We can’t send data off-network." -> Response: Offer on-prem package; outline minimal infra requirements and phased plan.
- Objection: "How do we validate model answers for bias/regulatory safety?" -> Response: We’ll run your eval set and wire outputs to your evaluation harness; link results to quality monitoring and regression alerts.
- Objection: "What about key control?" -> Response: KMS/HSM integration; we only store encrypted model artifacts and ephemeral decryption inside your VPC.

Demo flow (10–12 minutes):
1) Quick value pitch (60s) — show what pilot will measure.
2) Console: create pilot, attach KMS and audit config (120s) — real UI clicks or screenshots.
3) Run a simple query and show request trace + audit log exporting (120s).
4) Simulate region throttling -> show failover to fallback model/region (150s).
5) Cost/scale slide + next steps (90s).

Artifacts to produce for the customer during pilot:
- one-sheet: pilot charter + acceptance criteria (deliverable)
- evaluation dump (CSV) of N test prompts -> model outputs + confidence/metadata
- audit log export + SIEM ingestion guide
- cost delta analysis and recommended Dedicated/quantization plan

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Decide default quantized model for regulatory pilots (Samir to validate runbook).
- Create short checklist for on-prem air-gapped installs (Leah to draft).
- Confirm legal’s minimal contract addendum for pilot data handling (Diego to loop in).

Next steps for SEs using this card:
- Save a copy of the one-sheet, fill pilot charter during intro call, attach to JIRA GTMPILOT-142.
- Email security lead with KMS integration checklist and proposed timeline.
- Prepare a short demo recording (3–4 minutes) that highlights audit export and failover.

Notes to self (style/ tone):
- Keep language simple and audit-forward. Platform engineers care about exact signal names (trace_id, request_id) and retention windows.
- Avoid product buzzwords in the initial pitch — focus on guarantees (keys, regions, logs).

End.
